name: Wenzhan Li
intro: I study how robots can learn from experience, reason with world models, and adapt to a changing world.
bio: I am a Ph.D. student at Sun Yat-sen University, advised by Prof. Yulan Guo, with joint doctoral training at Shenzhen Loop Area Institute (SLAI). My research lies at the intersection of embodied AI, world-action models, and robot learning.
background: Previously, I worked on robotics algorithms at RoboSense and received my master's degree from Tsinghua University. I enjoy bringing research ideas through method design, code, and experiments to working robotic systems.
contact: I welcome conversations about robot learning, research collaborations, and research internships. If our interests overlap, I would be happy to connect.

news.label: Sep 2026
news.text: Started my Ph.D. at Sun Yat-sen University, with joint training at SLAI.
MERL, PAWN, and ComSim were accepted to CoRL 2026.

research.title: World models that support action
research.text: Learning representations of the world that make robotic action learning more useful and efficient.

research.title: Adaptation through experience
research.text: Studying how world-action models can improve through interaction, post-training, and the reuse of experience.

research.title: Learning across domains
research.text: Connecting simulation with real-world data and learning transferable representations across environments.

publications.title: Trust-Calibrated VLA Policy Post-Training with Evolving Imagination
publications.summary: Calibrating when and how a robot policy should trust an evolving world model during post-training.
publications.contribution: Led method design, research codebase development, experiments, and manuscript writing.
publications.imageAlt: A PiPER robot completing a block-to-box manipulation task in a MERL physical rollout.

publications.title: PAWN: Preference-Aware Semantic NFT for Online Reinforcement Learning of Flow-based VLAs
publications.summary: Structured local preferences for likelihood-free reinforcement learning of flow-based manipulation policies.
publications.contribution: Co-designed chunk scoring and continuation ranking; developed the chunk-scorer theory and proofs, and supported experiments and infrastructure.
publications.imageAlt: PAWN paper Figure 1 comparing local optimization signals for flow-based robot policies.

publications.title: Building Scalable Real-World Robot Data Generation via Compositional Simulation
publications.summary: Combining classical and neural simulation to generate action-aligned robot videos with real-world appearance.
publications.contribution: Implemented core action- and visual-conditioning components of the neural simulator; contributed experiments and writing.
publications.imageAlt: ComSim paper Figure 1 contrasting human-collected, classical-simulation, and neural-simulation data.

publications.title: Dual-Alignment Domain Adaptation for Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction
publications.summary: Data-level and feature-level alignment for pedestrian trajectory prediction across previously unseen scenes.
publications.contribution: Designed the dual-alignment method and developed the core algorithms and pipeline, with evaluation across ETH/UCY transfer tasks.
publications.imageAlt: DADA paper Figure 2 showing data-level and feature-level adversarial alignment.

education.detail: School of Electronics and Communication Engineering, Shenzhen Campus. Advised by Prof. Yulan Guo; joint doctoral training at SLAI / EACV.
Intelligent Manufacturing, Shenzhen International Graduate School.

experience.detail: AI Group, Decision-making Team. Model fine-tuning, annotation tooling, online/offline consistency, and field-test algorithm improvements.
Developed and evaluated a YOLOv3-based detector with BiFPN for restaurant scenes.

appointment.detail: World-model-based manipulation refinement and sim-to-real data generation. Contracted through The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen.

collaboration: I also contribute agent orchestration and memory mechanisms to a collaborative SLAI / EACV project on 3D indoor scene generation.
future: Looking ahead, I am interested in how heterogeneous robots might share knowledge and improve together across embodiments, environments, and tasks.
